slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
slot.brief: Electron (or alpha particle) accelerated through a given potential difference; compute its de Broglie wavelength directly via λ = h/√(2mqV).

stem: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of $100$ V. Find its de Broglie wavelength. Take $h=6.63\times10^{-34}$ J s, $m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}$ kg and $e=1.60\times10^{-19}$ C.

verdicts.working: The electron gains kinetic energy eV, so λ = h/√(2mₑeV) = 6.63×10⁻³⁴/√(2×9.11×10⁻³¹×1.60×10⁻¹⁷) ≈ 1.23×10⁻¹⁰ m.

working:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_e eV}}=\dfrac{6.63\times10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2(9.11\times10^{-31})(1.60\times10^{-19})(100)}}\approx1.23\times10^{-10}$ m.

Independent check: The electron gains kinetic energy eV, so λ = h/√(2mₑeV) = 6.63×10⁻³⁴/√(2×9.11×10⁻³¹×1.60×10⁻¹⁷) ≈ 1.23×10⁻¹⁰ m.
